title: Game view: when using another app on top of Godot, and moving pointer over active Game view, it takes focus (even behind another window)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 860M (nvidia; 535.183.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4710HQ CPU @ 2.50GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

When Godot is running the game in the new embedded game window aka Game view, and putting another app's window on front, and moving the mouse pointer above the Game view area (or it's equivalent behind the other application's window - imagine that the app window is transparent and you can see the Game view behind), the system will focus to Godot, and more specifically the Game view tab/viewport.

I'm not sure about the exact conditions to trigger it, at one time I tried to reproduce it and it didn't happen. The next time, I found that focusing the Game view viewport instead of the Remote tree helps triggering the bug, but the 3rd time it didn't happen even in these conditions.

Either way, the bug is very annoying as I was writing a bug report and since my Game view is very big, it covers most of my screen and so my mouse which was moving over my browser page area kept sending focus to Godot and unfocus my browser.

In the video below, I'm repeatedly clicking to focus the browser, but since my mouse is over the Game view area behind, I immediately lose focus again. At the end I click in the above area (browser toolbar/titlebar) to regain focus, but as soon as I move the pointer down, Game view catches focus again.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d0a86fe-5220-4116-844d-7eb5b96c9ce8

In fact, even when the mouse pointer is hovering a part that is not covered by the front app, I don't expect focus to switch from the app to Godot.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Play a dummy game
2. Stretch the game view to cover enough space to easily trigger the bug
3. Open a browser or another app on top of Godot
4. Move your mouse pointer above the Game view area (covered by the app window, or not)
